judge_notes.opus: C won because it is the only summary that interprets as well as reports: it builds a throughline around 'gain' ('OpenAI and AMD reported a different kind of gain') and explains the deal's logic ('betting that enterprises will want to adapt open-weight models as well as buy access to closed ones'). Its only real weakness is that the IPO gets one thin sentence. L and S follow, L for the record-IPO context ('The raise tops SpaceX's June listing') and S for its framing line 'Recursive self-improvement is moving into policy.' M finished last: it buries the news under specs and acronyms ('rewrote SystemVerilog RTL to achieve up to 14% power, performance, and area gains on flagship AMD GPU IP') and fills its middle with the generic 'Enterprise M&A and hardware-focused AI also posted major milestones.'
judge_notes.astra: J wins because “Neon finished faster than Carbon at a lower standard-price cost per task” translates benchmarking into practical value, and “betting that enterprises will want to adapt open-weight models” interprets the acquisition. It still has a disconnected IPO item, so earns 4 rather than 5. G loses because “rewrote SystemVerilog RTL” sits inside a massive multi-story sentence with “flagship AMD GPU IP”; its technical and numerical stacking makes the paragraph hard work.
judge_notes.grok: T won because it is the only summary with a concrete throughline and no run-on, hedge, or broken clause: "an independent test points to a practical gain," then "a different kind of gain," including designs "engineers had already spent years optimizing" and a buyer "betting that enterprises will want to adapt open-weight models." The bare IPO sentence keeps it off a 5. I lost because nothing in it is specific enough to repeat: "a new model aimed at coding and knowledge work," "described AI-assisted chip design work," "published new internal measurements," then a closer on what the news is not, "The proposals are not yet enacted requirements."
judge_notes.dsflash: V wins on hierarchy and tension: it opens with the number that makes the day matter, "at $83 per share, above its $70 to $78 range," then supplies conflict rather than another spec, "which argues Anthropic's safety branding conflicts with its race to build recursively self-improving AI." G is close behind for the only two sentences in the set that explain consequence, "Neon finished faster than Carbon at a lower standard-price cost per task" and "betting that enterprises will want to adapt open-weight models as well as buy access to closed ones," but it starves the IPO to one clause, "priced its IPO at $83 a share ahead of expected Nasdaq trading." C is the cleanest short piece with a real throughline, "Recursive self-improvement is moving into policy," though it asserts authority instead of earning it, "is the day's main model release." The bottom is F, whose opener runs five clauses before a verb lands, "pricing API access at $3/$15 per million tokens while taking third place... and second on the Agent Arena Index alongside the rollout of Genie 4," and N, which stacks scaffolding on top of jargon, "Enterprise M&A and hardware-focused AI also posted major milestones" then "rewrote SystemVerilog RTL to achieve up to 14% power, performance, and area gains." Both read as press-release digest, not editing.
